snippet.title: Nerve Ease Reviews and Dr. Ohsumi AI Video Scam Exposed
snippet.description:
This video reports on the fact that any consumers searching for Nerve Ease reviews should be aware of a supplements scam. Dr. Ben Carson and Dr. Yoshinori Ohsumi never backed Nerve Ease advanced nerve support capsules, nor any "Japanese cocktail" recipe to cure neuropathy. No miracle recipe exists to end nerve pain or neuropathy.

My name is Jordan Liles. I am a senior reporter with Snopes.com by day. I came here to my YouTube channel on nights and weekends to help consumers stay away from scams. In my investigation, I found scammers marketed Nerve Ease using a deceptive website they designed to look like the official page for the Nobel Prize. That website featured an incredibly lengthy video presentation with deepfake AI depictions of Drs. Yoshinori Ohsumi and Ben Carson. No doctors, hospitals, universities or famous people ever endorsed Nerve Ease capsules, gummies, pills or supplements.

The scammers used a classic scam hook to influence consumers into watching the incredibly long video presentation. The video initially promises a recipe using common pantry ingredients. Scammers know consumers won't stick around if they introduce a bottle of pills at the very beginning of the presentation. So instead, they lie and dangle a recipe promise for over an hour. By the end of the video, the scammers offer a bottle of Nerve Ease supplements — including featuring a fake Nerve Ease reviews score of 4.9 out of 5.

In the past, I've found scams similar to the Nerve Ease supplements offer to hide subscription charges of hundreds of dollars per month. Also, some money-back guarantees might not be honored. Surprise, surprise.

Anyone victimized by this scam should file a complaint with the Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) via IC3.gov. Include as many details as possible, such as any names, mailing addresses, phone numbers and email addresses appearing in correspondence or on your bank or credit card statements. Also, feature in your complaint how you discovered the ads for the scam, link to the website where the scam took you to, etc. Every detail is important.

My name is Jordan Liles. I am a senior reporter with Snopes.com by day. I come here to my YouTube channel on nights and weekends to help consumers stay away from scams. Ads and a lengthy inauthentic "60 Minutes" video on the fake Fox News website falsely claimed Dr. William Li formulated or endorsed Glycotide, including mentioning something about Harvard Medical School being involved.
